timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna had spent eight months missing Dante. Since taking his watch from Valentino's glove compartment the night she killed him, she'd slept in it, showered in it, and hit a man with it. Nigga, a timepiece that had done everything except tell her what was inside it. I noticed because I was jealous of the motherfucker.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I'd studied that watch across tables, across beds, underneath her hand on my cheek. When the inner clasp shifted against her thumbnail, I saw a seam. "Wait. There's something there." She held it under the lamp. "Where?" "There.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, that bit moved." "You know how this opens?" "No." "Then give me back my watch before you become the next thing I hit with it." I surrendered it. "A nigga makes a discovery, suddenly the museum throws him out." Shawna called Rosa for a jeweler she trusted. I heard the answer from beside her. "Trusted to do what, bitch?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Those are different men." "Open a watch without breaking it." "Oh. I got that nigga. He owes me money." "That makes him trustworthy?" I asked. "It makes him findable. Do you want reliable or do you want found?" "Send the findable nigga." An hour later the jeweler sat at our table, turning the clasp beneath his loupe. I reached for the watch once.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna moved it away without looking at me. "Who built this?" he asked. "Marcellus Vale." He lowered the loupe. "You know where he is?" "Prison," she said. "He got out nine days ago. Came to my shop asking about his old bench." Shawna grabbed my arm. I put my hand over hers. "Nigga, call him." "I'm not—" "Then call him whatever you are.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Just call the fucking man." "I was going to say I'm not certain he answers this number." Shawna looked at me. "Your nigga is excited," I said. "Your nigga is going to let the man dial," she said. I sat back. The jeweler dialed. Marcellus said almost nothing until Shawna took the phone and gave her name.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then I heard him clearly from across the table. "Dante's wife?" She covered her mouth and nodded. I touched her wrist. She remembered he couldn't see her. "Yes." I kept quiet while she spoke to him. Nigga, for once I knew which part belonged to me. I held her other hand. The old nigga came before sunset.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He was sixty-two, tall and narrow, with close gray hair and a brown coat that didn't suit the weather. He carried a paper bag containing a clean shirt. Everything else he'd owned was apparently somewhere he couldn't get to anymore. He had barely reached the gate when three men got out of a car behind him. I saw it from the front steps.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The old man stopped. The tallest of the three caught his coat, and the paper bag fell out of his hand. Nigga, I had just paid to have my gate repaired after Roman's people. Now another set of niggas had decided my driveway was the place to finish a conversation.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Tank!" He came out of the side door with a piece of bread in his mouth. Saw the gate. Took the bread out. "Those your jeweler's friends?" "They holding him like enemies." Shawna was behind me before I reached the steps. She saw the old man and stopped breathing for a second. "Marcellus." I looked back at her. Then I went to get her nigga.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The tall man had Marcellus against the bars. Thirty-five or so, purple suit, pale scar on his cheek, rings on every finger except the one he'd apparently decided needed to stay humble. "Go inside," he told me. "Nigga, I came outside for you. Don't make the trip disappointing." He glanced at Tank and readjusted his grip on the old man's coat.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Private business." "My private gate. See how a nigga keeps turning up in your problem?" One of the other men opened his jacket. A pistol showed against his belt. I looked at it. Then back at the man. "That's nice. You buy a second one for when that one leaves you?" He pulled it. Tank moved before it cleared the jacket.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Hit the man against the car so hard the back window broke. The third man swung at me. I caught his shoulder, turned with him, and put him face-first into the stone pillar beside the gate. The tall man dragged Marcellus in front of himself. A gun appeared against the old man's coat. Everything stopped.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I could hear Shawna behind me say, "Don't." I didn't know whether she meant me or him. The old man looked past the gun at the paper bag on the ground. His clean shirt lay in the dust. "Pick it up," Marcellus said. The tall man blinked. "What?" "My shirt." "Nigga, you out your fucking mind?" "No," Marcellus said. "I've been out nine days.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: That is the only shirt I have bought." The nigga holding him looked at me, as if he expected somebody reasonable to explain why the situation wasn't respecting his gun. I held out one hand. "Let him get the shirt." "You think I'm stupid?" "Nigga, I'm giving you a chance to surprise me." He pulled Marcellus back another step.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The old man's shoe caught his bag. He stumbled, and for half a second the gun moved away from his chest. I hit the gate with both hands. It swung hard into them. Metal struck the tall man's arm. The gun went off into the driveway, kicking a white chip out of the stone. Marcellus dropped.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I caught the man's wrist against the bars and held it there while he tried to turn toward me. Nigga, his rings were pretty. His bones were ordinary. The gun fell. I drove him into the gate again and let him slide down it. Tank had the other two on the ground. One was cussing. The other was reconsidering breathing loudly.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna ran past me to Marcellus and got her hands under his arms. "You hurt?" "My coat." "Fuck the coat. Are you hurt?" He shook his head. Mercedes came through the gate with the clean shirt in her hands. She'd taken it off the ground while everybody else was watching me. She brushed the dust from its sleeves and held it up to the sunlight.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Little wash," she told him. "You're handsome again." The old man looked at her like he hadn't been spoken to that gently in years. I turned back to the nigga on the ground. "Who are you?" "Felix." "Felix what?" "Barrow." "What you want with him?" Felix swallowed. He kept looking at his empty hand. "He owes people." "Which people?" "People inside. He made things.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Things got promised." I looked at Marcellus. The old man shook his head once. "I promised him nothing." "There you go," I told Felix. "Nigga ain't got your promise. You ain't got your gun. Everybody learned something." Felix looked past me at the house, the cars, the women standing with the old man, Tank holding two grown men down with one look.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "You're that Aiden." "Which one you hoping for?" "The boat. The hearse." "Nigga, you're behind. There's two boats." Mercedes laughed. Tank did too. Even Marcellus looked at me a little differently, like Shawna's six repetitions of my name had finally found enough room to stand. Felix put his head back against the bars.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "I should've asked where he was going." "Nigga, you should've stayed home." Knox's men came for the three of them. Tank called. I didn't ask what he said. I was busy taking Marcellus inside while Shawna held one of his hands and Mercedes carried his clean shirt like the nigga had arrived with a flag.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: At the door, the old man stopped and looked up at me. "Dante would've liked you." "Nigga, everybody gets there. Some men just take the long way." He smiled then. Small, but real. The whole hard face opened enough that I could see the man Celeste must have come home to before anybody took anything.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Apparently," he said, "I came to the right house." I introduced myself properly at the front door. Aiden. I know. People talking? Dante's widow said your name six times on the telephone. I liked the old nigga right then. He looked at the cross on my chest. He touched it once, with a fingertip. I did those letters.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Dante sent the cross in with the watch. Said his wife thought he was magnificent, and the nigga wasn't arguing. Then come inside. Nigga, Shawna crossed the room too fast and stopped just short of him. For a second neither of them knew what to do. Then he put the paper bag down and opened his arms. She cried against his coat.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I watched the old nigga's hand settle carefully between her shoulders. His eyes closed. He hadn't seen Dante die. Neither had she. They had each kept a different part of him alive, and now they were standing in my expensive fucking living room discovering the other part had been real. My nigga Tank came back from the gate carrying a bag of food.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He saw them, lowered the bag, and went quiet. Who this? he asked me. Marcellus. Tank looked toward the door. The old nigga looked at Tank's face for a long second. Your friend? he asked me. Yeah. I see. He didn't say anything else. Tank put the food down and went back outside. Marcellus opened the watch while we waited at the table.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: My nigga worked with the patience of a man who had spent years having nowhere to hurry. Dante had asked him about a place to keep a letter when they were still inside. After Dante got out, a watch had reached Marcellus through a legal repair commission arranged by an old client. He had made the clasp for him and sent it back.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I let the old man finish telling me that because I wanted to hear Dante had planned to live long enough to read whatever he hid. Nigga, a thin folded piece of paper lay inside. Marcellus set it on the table. He put his hands flat beside it and didn't touch it again. Shawna opened it. The paper had been torn from a longer note.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Red ink. The same slanted, crowded handwriting I'd been holding in the car that morning. T — He has the withdrawal and Vale's story. If he gets the stone, he can name every one of us. Finish Dante tonight. No more brother shit. Valentino takes the watch. Keep her alive. I'll deal with her. R. Underneath, in darker ink, Dante had written four words. Shawna.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: If I'm wrong. She read it twice. The third time she didn't finish. No, she said. I reached for her hand. She pulled away and stood so quickly the chair fell over. No. He knew? Marcellus watched the note. He suspected. He fucking knew. I picked up the paper, and everything in me went still. Nigga, there wasn't a word on it about protecting her.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: There wasn't a word about Valentino acting alone. Red had ordered a man's death and chosen where the widow would go before the body was cold. I heard the nigga saying he'd bought her dress. I heard the nigga saying the piano was still there. Nigga, I said very quietly. Marcellus looked at me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I had no idea which of those dead motherfuckers Dante had taken that note from. I didn't know why he hadn't run the minute he read it. He had still written if, like he could find some version of those words that didn't mean what they meant. I knew that part. T had put his hand on my neck and called me son.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I had been ready to believe the nigga right up until he told me to fetch Shawna. She was standing by the window with both hands on her head. He went to talk to his brother, she said. He told me there was a mistake he had to straighten out. I was mad because he wouldn't stay for dinner. Marcellus closed his eyes.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I told him I'd throw his plate away. I got up. Shawna. Don't say it. I wasn't— Don't fucking say there was nothing I could do. I could've locked the door. I could've gone with him. I could've— You could've died too. She slapped me. Hard. Right across the mouth that still wasn't properly healed.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I stood there with blood coming back onto my tongue. Her hand stayed in the air. Aiden. I took a breath through my nose. The whole room was waiting for me to become the worst man in it. Nigga, I reached for her wrist, lowered her hand, and let go. I'm going outside. I went outside.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank was by the lake throwing pieces of bread to the birds. The nigga looked up when he saw my mouth. What happened? Don't. My nigga put the bread down. I stood beside him until I could breathe without wanting to break something that had cost me money. She hit you? Nigga, I said don't. All right.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, a bird walked up between us and took the whole remaining roll. Tank watched it go. That was mine. Go tell him. He didn't move. Nigga, I almost laughed. It hurt too much, so I sat on the low wall instead. Red ordered it, I told him. Dante. We got his own fucking handwriting. Tank stared at the water. You know? No.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: You heard anything? I heard Dante took money. And that's all? That was all anybody was saying around me. He looked at me finally. I didn't know him like that. T had me moving things. Driving people. I wasn't in every room. I wanted to believe the nigga.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I wanted somebody I loved to tell me a complete fucking thing before another man handed me the part they'd left out. I'm taking Red's diamond, I said. Tank's jaw shifted. And then? And then I'm going to look at how poor the motherfucker got. Forty million ain't all he has. Then I'll stay busy. The back door opened.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna came out carrying a wet cloth. She had taken Dante's watch off. It was in her other hand. Tank picked up the empty bread bag and walked away. She stood in front of me. I shouldn't have done that. No shit. Can I see? I let her touch my chin.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She cleaned the blood off my mouth, and I looked past her because I was still too angry to look at her without saying something cruel. I love him, she said. I fucking know, Shawna. I love you too. You tell him that before he left? I asked. She shook her head. I was mad about dinner. I looked at her then.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: She put the cloth down and touched my face with her empty hand. I love you, she said again. Nigga, I took her hand and pressed it against my chest so she could feel what the shit was doing to me. Don't hit me again. I won't. And don't take that watch off because you think it'll shut me up. Put it back on.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I want the whole thing when you tell me something. She looked down at it. Then she put it back on. We ate the food my nigga Tank had bought. Marcellus kept Celeste's old letter beside his plate in a clear sleeve. He let me read it while he ate.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: When I gave it back, he put it inside his coat with the same careful movement Shawna used with Dante's photograph. You want your stone? I asked him. Yes. You want Red dead? He looked at Shawna. Yes. Nigga, I think we can work together. He didn't smile. Shawna laid the invitations on the table. He's putting it on display in three nights.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Marcellus picked one up. The front showed a blue necklace I recognized from Shawna's description. He's putting something on display, he said. There's two, I said. Yes. You tell them apart? Of course. Then you're going. He knows my face. He knows the face he put in prison eight years ago. We'll give you another suit and somebody else's name.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Rosa, who had come back while we were eating, looked at him. I know a woman who can make you look like a man with money. Marcellus looked around my dining room. Apparently it's easy to confuse people. Tank covered his mouth with his napkin. I let the old nigga have that one. He'd been through a lot. There are different settings, Marcellus said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The blue outer mounting can be removed. A buyer might wear the stone another way. The original has a flaw inside it. Very small. I remember exactly where it is. The copy doesn't. But the necklace in the picture? Shawna asked. Could hold either. I sat back. Then we get you close enough to look. Red wanted her back.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: That was the part we had that forty million dollars couldn't buy him. He wanted Shawna walking into his room while other men watched. Nigga, he wanted every motherfucker who'd heard she left him to see her choose him instead. Shawna knew it too. I can get him to invite us closer, she said. No. Aiden. No. You haven't heard what I'm saying.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I heard it in the way you sat up. She reached across the table and took my hand. I tell him I made a mistake. That you scare me. That I'm bringing you to the gala because I want him to handle it quietly. Tank looked at her. And he believes that? He wants to. My fingers tightened around hers. What else?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I tell him I know where your money is. I don't have his fucking money. He doesn't know that. Tank put his glass down a little too carefully. I was watching Shawna. I missed it until later. Tell him I'm tired of running, she said. Tell him I'll come back if he clears the debt and leaves you alive.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, why he going to leave me alive? Because I'm going to say you can give him the west side. I let go of her hand. The room went quiet again. She leaned toward me. I'm saying what he'll listen to. You know that. I did know. It still felt like watching her put on the dress he'd bought.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Marcellus folded the invitation and set it down. If he believes she can give you to him, he'll want you close enough to take. Then he can fucking try. Rosa looked at Shawna. You get near the jewel, the old man looks at it, we leave with what's his. You do not decide to kill somebody in the middle because you get mad.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna said nothing. Rosa pointed at me. You either. Nigga, why everybody looking at me? Because you have the face, she said. Tank nodded as if that settled it. Shawna made the call from our bedroom with me sitting beside her. Red answered on the second ring. There she is. She closed her eyes. I put my hand on her knee. Can you talk?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: For you? Nigga, I wanted to take the phone and put it through the fucking wall. I left my hand where it was. I think I made a mistake, she said. Red didn't answer immediately. Outside, the lake had gone black. Our reflection floated in the window: her with the phone, me beside her like a man waiting for a verdict. He hurt you?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Red asked. Nigga, she looked at the cut on my mouth. I don't know what he's going to do next. Come home. I can't just leave. Yes, you can. You want the money. You want his streets. I can bring him to you, Red. But you have to promise me something. Anything. The ease of it made me sick.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The nigga had put a man's death in a note shorter than the promises he was making to his widow. You let him live, she said. Red sighed. You're too good to these boys. Nigga, my hand left her knee. My nigga, she caught it before I could stand. I know where he's keeping the money, she said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I can get him to bring what you need. At the gala, I'll stay close to you. Everybody can see I'm back. After that, you talk to him. And you stay? She looked at me. Yes. Red let out a breath into the phone. Nigga, I heard the pleasure in it. I heard how badly the nigga had wanted to win.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Wear the blue dress, he said. The one I liked. I will. And Shawna? What? I knew you'd remember who loved you. She hung up without answering. I knew it was a lie. I had helped make it. Every fucking word still hurt. She took my face in both hands. Look at me, Aiden. I did. I'm here.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I pulled her into me, too hard, and my side burned. I held on anyway. Downstairs, the old man was measuring the empty space where his wife's diamond ought to have been. Tank was on the phone with somebody he wasn't ready to name. Rosa was choosing a dress that would make a killer forget the last thing he'd been careful about. And me?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I was holding my woman and imagining forty million dollars in one hand, Red's whole fucking life in the other. Three nights. Nigga, I could wait three nights. I told myself that until morning.
